findings.text: TDX virtual CPU exit handling is offered as a routine that consumes a virtual CPU plus a fast-path hint and reports how to proceed among resume, leave to user space, or fail with an IO error on detected inconsistency. It screens module return status for configuration, software and entry failures before routing the architectural exit reason to dedicated emulation or to a generic unexpected path.

The generic VMX exit entry wraps the inner handler and adds bus-lock promotion. When the exit reason carries a bus-lock indication the user-visible reason becomes a bus-lock exit whenever inner handling would have resumed, the bus-lock flag is always set in run flags, and control returns to user space. Otherwise the inner result is preserved.

After pre-checks the TDX path selects behavior by basic exit class. Emulated operations cover processor identification, halt, trust-domain calls, hypercalls, port IO, model-specific register access and memory-mapped IO. Fault and event classes cover shutdown, exception with non-maskable delegation, counted external interrupts, EPT violation handling and system-management resumes. Any class outside the recognized set falls through to unexpected-reason preparation.

The common VMX path applies an ordered prologue before reason dispatch. It flushes page-modification logging when enabled outside guest mode, honors a request to leave directly to user space, treats pending nested entry as fatal, reflects or synthesizes nested exits while running nested guests while marking nested control pages dirty, diverts invalid guest state to emulation, and converts failed entry or launch failure into a fail-entry exit carrying reason and CPU.

The TDX pre-dispatch screen enforces several contracts. A non-idle fast-path hint forces resume without further work. An entry return indicating misconfiguration is treated as a host bug and fatal. A software-error pattern is treated as a host bug unless rebooting. Failed entry produces a fail-entry exit with hardware reason and CPU. Other error or non-recoverable indications outside triple fault are logged as unimplemented and treated as unexpected, while success status is expected outside triple fault.

Exception and non-maskable exits resume the guest when the interruption information denotes a non-maskable interrupt or a machine check. All other vectors leave to user space as an exception exit carrying the vector number and a zero error code. Machine-check detection is defined as the exception vector for machine check.

Processor identification emulation takes leaf from enter argument R12 and subleaf from R13, invokes the common CPUID helper without faulting, writes the four result words back into enter arguments R12 through R15, and resumes the guest.

Hypercall bridging copies five enter-argument registers into guest general registers for accumulator through source index, then invokes generic hypercall emulation with a completion helper for exits. The mapping preserves R10 into accumulator, R11 into base, R12 into count, R13 into data and R14 into source index.

Port IO emulation counts the exit and interprets size, direction and port from enter arguments. It rejects directions outside read or write and widths outside the allowed set with an invalid-operand return code while resuming. Otherwise it performs emulated port input or output and arms a direction-specific completion when user-space continuation is required. Synchronous reads publish the value through the return-value channel.

Memory-mapped IO emulation validates width and direction, rejects private ranges and values outside the allowed sets with invalid operand while resuming, strips direct-mapping bits from the address, attempts fast then regular IO buses for writes and the regular bus for reads with tracing, and on miss prepares a user-space emulated IO exit with write flag and read completion state including fragment address and length.

Trust-domain call handling supports mapping an address range, reporting fatal errors, querying call information, obtaining attestation quotes and configuring event notification. Any other leaf reports unsupported subfunction and resumes.

Range mapping requires that user space opted into hypercall exits for the mapping hypercall, otherwise it reports unsupported. It rejects address overflow, illegal addresses, mixed private-shared spans and unaligned address or length with operand or alignment errors while echoing the address. On success it initializes a cursor over the range and emits the first bounded chunk as a long-mode hypercall exit with masked address, page count, encryption flag and a mapping completion.

Fatal-error reporting leaves to user space as a system event of TDX fatal type with sixteen data slots, populated from the module return value, selected enter-argument registers and the low module registers, with two middle slots forced to zero and ordering following ascending general-register order.

Call-information query with selector zero completes in kernel by clearing four return registers and reporting success. Selector one forwards to user space as a TDX exit carrying leaf, zero flags and cleared result fields with a dedicated completion. Any other selector reports invalid operand and resumes.

Quote retrieval requires a shared buffer address, otherwise invalid operand. On success it forwards to user space as a TDX exit with masked address, size and an initially unsupported status plus a simple completion. Event-notification setup validates the vector range, then similarly forwards with vector and simple completion.

EPT violation handling separates private and shared addresses. Private faults that arrive before acceptance while an unexpected pending violation is signaled kill the virtual machine and fail. Other private faults ignore reported qualification, force write semantics and enable local retry to reduce entry invocations and mitigation contention. Shared faults use reported qualification but treat instruction fetch as fatal. The handler traces the fault then loops on retryable faults while checking for pending events, signals, VM-dead requests and invalid memslots, yielding the scheduler between attempts.

Accepted guest operand sets include port IO widths of one two and four, memory-mapped IO widths of one two four and eight, direction zero for read and one for write, event-notification vectors from thirty two through two five five inclusive, fatal-event payload of sixteen entries, and mapping chunks bounded by a maximum length with page-granular counts.

Trust-domain call result channels are fixed enter-argument slots with return code in R10 and return value in R11. Operand inputs use R12 onward, with CPUID leaf and subleaf, IO size direction port and write data, MMIO size direction address and write data, mapping address and length, quote address and length, and notification vector all carried in those slots.

Observed per-vCPU TDX state groups a module return value with an argument block, an exit address, an extended qualification and a mapping cursor. Identifiers seen include vp_enter_ret, vp_enter_args, exit_gpa, ext_exit_qualification, map_gpa_next and map_gpa_end alongside vcpu and run, with run carrying exit reason, hypercall details, MMIO staging and completion callbacks plus TDX specific payloads.
